messages:
elaine: FYI I'm seeing sustained tail spikes on apac-edge-3 GPU hosts. Looks like some tenant traffic is getting an extra transit hop and filling egress queues :grimacing:
raj: can you drop the traceroute + any exabgp logs? sound like AS-path diversion or an accidental community we pushed
elaine: traceroute to 10.22.9.8 (10.22.9.8), 8 hops max
 1 10.22.0.1 0.38 ms 0.31 ms 0.29 ms
 2 10.22.1.6 1.00 ms 0.98 ms 1.02 ms
 3 198.51.100.12 13.4 ms 13.2 ms 13.3 ms
 4 203.0.113.5 47.9 ms 48.1 ms 48.0 ms
 5 10.22.9.8 48.0 ms 47.8 ms 48.2 ms
elaine: noisy tenant is t-7b4c, p99 tail for infer nodes up ~600-900ms, pattern is bursty with 30s on/2m off
marta: infra-bot fired earlier: "infra-bot: apac-edge-3 egress_queue_depth=73% for 14m, nodes edge-gpu-12..edge-gpu-14 impacted"
raj: we did a small AS-path prepend change yesterday to shift more trafffic to cheaper transit. Could be that prepends + burst => longer path during congestion
elaine: rollback of BGP change would hit our transit bill but might be faster. Alternative: steer that tenant to apac-dedicated-pool-1 for 12-24h and throttle at proxy layer
tom: cost tradeoff: dedicated carve will incur warmup GPU-hours and might reduce capacity for reserved customers. But rollback might cost more if traffic volume stays high for days
marta: we can do policy steer: `route-policy TENANT_T7B4C permit 10; set next-hop 10.23.0.3` — need `routing:modify` to apply
raj: estimate: steer => +10 GPU-hours prefill, ~0.5% pool usage for 24h. Rollback => transit delta estimated +$120/day on current rates. Steering seems cheaper short term
elaine: applied steer via API: POST /api/v1/routing/tenants/t-7b4c/steer payload: {"target_pool":"apac-dedicated-pool-1","ttl_hours":"24"} (used change_id c-9921)
infra-bot: infra-bot: routing change applied for t-7b4c -> apac-dedicated-pool-1, change_id c-9921
elaine: starting targeted telemetry: sampling KV cache size, egress_q depth, p50/p95/p99.
marta: added soft proxy throttle: `proxy.throttle.set('t-7b4c', rps=180, burst=40)` and enabled `kvcache.eviction=aggressive` for that pool
infra-bot: metric snapshot (1m after steer): egress_queue_depth apac-edge-3 before=73% after=38%
elaine: p99 on affected hosts dropped 820ms -> 210ms in first 10m window :partyparrot:
tom: good improvement. Watch for headroom on dedicated pool and alert if dedicated_util > 85%
raj: also enabled prefix_kvcache_trim to reduce long lived cache entries that were inflating memory usage on those VMs
elaine: 30m update: egress_queue stable ~36%, KV miss rate improved ~12%, tail p99 ~190ms. No regressions so far
tom: can we quantify tomorrow's cost if tenant behaves like this continuously? We should present options: enforced dedicated carve, sustained throttle + surcharge, or roll BGP rollback
raj: I'll run a cost runbook and post numbers in morning. Rough: sustained steering + warmup ~+20 GPU-hours/day vs rollback transit delta ~+$120/day; needs exact numbers per region
marta: added auto-unsteer at 2025-07-04T08:00Z unless infra approves extension, and alert: if egress_queue_depth > 60% OR p99 > 400ms -> auto-unsteer + page #oncall
elaine: agree rollback should be last resort. We need a control plane playbook: 1) steer noisy tenant to dedicated 2) proxy throttle 3) enable aggressive kvcache eviction/prefix trim 4) only rollback BGP if multiple tenants or persistent across racks
raj: filing INFRA-1182 "apac edge AS-path steering risk assessment" assign->raj, include cost vs latency curves, and mitigation checklist
elaine: thanks all, monitoring on. ping here if anything spikes back up :wave:
